openings.claim: Transfer sideways restraint from seal friction to removable locating bolts carried by two padded strip saddles. A separate, balanced hold-down setting may avoid the observed opposite-corner lift. Neither attachment capacity nor success is supplied.
openings.delta: Drill only strips; bolt them as two upper/lower rim saddles using four bolts and four pads. Use the remaining bolts as hatch-edge locators along the pull direction; tether recoverable parts with cord. Release and move saddles entirely outside the marked opening. Nearest rival: straps increasing normal force and relying on seal friction.
openings.prediction: Locators predict less sideways displacement without increased corner compression; the friction rival predicts restraint changing with compression. Defeat: saddles move, locator clearance exceeds 1 mm, disturbed closure rocks, reopening exceeds 30 seconds, or seal damage appears. Locating along the pull direction alone does not establish repeatability in the other direction.
openings.probe: Confirm accessible rim underside, locator reach, reversible pad seating and full open clearance before fabrication. Within twelve closure/pull trials, run ten candidate cycles, including a disturbed final closure; measure position, 20 N displacement, reopening time and visible seal condition. Reserve two disturbed trials for the feedback comparison, with equal initial closure setting and 20 N demand. A comparison counts only if the stated return response can be varied safely and measurably.
assumptions: Rim access, strip/bolt geometry, cord anchorage and clamp capacity are indispensable unknowns; supplied strips may not form these saddles within ninety minutes.

Hypothesized arrows: friction-dependent restraint mechanism → demand for extra compression after slip; demand → technician left-corner tightening response; response → mechanism through opposite-corner lift and reduced contact. Only tightening → lift is supplied; the other arrows and friction effect remain hypotheses.

Remove slip-triggered extra tightening without removing inspection access or restraint, using preset balanced closure. Sham retains that return rule with identical initial demand. No return influence: displacement and corner lift do not differ beyond ruler resolution. Invalid sham execution leaves the loop unresolved.

assessment: Bounded feasibility and discrimination probe; unknown geometry prevents a deployment claim. Ten-cycle success must satisfy every stated outcome, including disturbed position, pull resistance and reopening.
